canonical_topic: Two-trade structure: Henry Hub futures + basis swap
definition: Physical natural gas trading is typically executed as two separate trades — a liquid, standardized Henry Hub futures trade, followed by a basis swap that converts the Henry Hub exposure into exposure at the desired delivery location.
core_idea: The market is structured around a highly liquid, standardized Henry Hub futures contract precisely to make it easy to find counterparties, with the harder-to-trade locational piece handled separately via a basis swap.
key_points: Henry Hub futures are exchange-traded, standardized contracts that are very liquid — large volumes trade quickly with minimal transaction costs.
It is much harder to find counterparties willing to trade at other, non-Henry-Hub locations directly.
Exchange-traded Henry Hub futures eliminate counterparty credit risk concerns and allow trades to be netted.
Traders execute the bulk of their volume at Henry Hub first, then complete the locational piece once a suitable basis counterparty is found.
relationships: Combines the index price (Henry Hub futures) with the basis price (basis swap) to reconstruct an all-in locational exposure.
trading_implications: Expect better liquidity and tighter costs trading Henry Hub futures than trading directly at illiquid delivery points.
Locational (basis) trades may face longer time-to-execution due to thinner counterparty availability.
caveats: Assuming all natural gas locations trade with Henry-Hub-like liquidity — most do not.
